source_text:
5.12 Καὶ εὐφρανθήτωσαν ἐπὶ σοὶ πάν τες οἱ ἐλπίζοντες ἐπὶ
σὲ, εἰς αἰῶνα ἀγαλ λιάσονται, καὶ κατασκηνώσεις ἐν αὐτοῖς.
Τῶν ἐπιβούλων
καταλυθέντων, ἡ εὐφρο σύνη σοῦ κατασκηνοῦντος ἐν αὐτοῖς εἰς αἰῶ να. Καὶ πῶς
γὰρ οὐκ ἀγαλλίασις, ῳ Θεὸς πάρεστιν, ὡς ἐν ἰδίῳ ναῷ ἐνοικῶν τε καὶ περιπατῶν;
ὡς τὸ μακρύνεσθαι Θεοῦ, τῆς ἁμαρτίας αἰχμαλωτιζούσης, θρήνων ἐπάξιον. Τέλος
δὲ τῶν ἀγαθῶν, ἀπολαβεῖν κληρονο μίαν καὶ κλῆρον ε χειν ἐνοικοῦντα Θεόν.
pass_a_gloss: And let-them-be-glad upon you all the ones-hoping upon you, into age they-will-exult, and you-will-tabernacle in them. Of-the plotters having-been-dissolved, the gladness of-you tabernacling in them into age. And how for not exultation, to-whom God is-present, as in own temple dwelling both and walking? as the to-be-far of-God, of-the sin taking-captive, of-laments worthy. End and of-the good-things, to-receive inheritance and lot to-have dwelling God.
pass_b_english: “And let all who hope on you be glad in you; they will exult forever, and you will tabernacle in them” (Psalm 5:12).

When the plotters have been dissolved, the gladness is of you tabernacling in them forever. And how is it not exultation, for the one to whom God is present, dwelling and walking as in his own temple (2 Corinthians 6:16)? As being far from God, when sin takes captive, is worthy of lamentations. And the end of the good things is to receive an inheritance and to have as a lot God dwelling [in one].

choices.why: Future of κατασκηνόω, God as the one pitching tent in them. Not ‘you will overshadow’.
Paul’s temple wording (2 Cor 6:16), as in 5.8 the temple is Christ. Not mere presence.
